        Product Info Manual

        The mobile-friendly web version of the manual — the text fits your screen, so you just scroll. Tap a section to open it, or search below. This is the version to read on a phone.

        Version 2026.11.04.15 Web edition — matches the app

        Need it on paper? Use Product Info Manual — PDF (for printing) in Documents, directly below the web manual entry. It has the same content, laid out as fixed pages for printing.

        Jump to

        No section matches that search Try a shorter word — for example love, scan, price, admin or store — or tap Clear to see the whole manual again.
        1Getting startedOpen the app, pick your store, find your way around

        WR Product Info is the shared wine list for Wine Rack stores. Everyone using it sees the same products, prices and notes — when one person fixes something, it is fixed for everybody.

        First time you open it

        1. A popup asks “Which store are you at?”
        2. Pick your store from the list, or use Add store to create a new one.
        3. A brand-new store starts with no products ticked. Go to Settings → Set store products and tick what your store carries.
        You don’t need to sign in to browseThe full list, search, filters, scanner, Settings and Documents all work signed out. Signing in is only needed to love wines and to add or edit anything — so your loves are yours and your changes carry your name. See §11.

        The tabs at the top

        • Products — the wine list, search and filters. This is where you’ll spend most of your time.
        • Documents — Loved wines, this manual, impact cheat sheets and support information.
        • Settings — your account and sign-in, display name, appearance, store settings and the Support Center.

        Header, at a glance

        • The store pill (just the number, e.g. 358) sits beside the heading — tap it to switch stores.
        • The Food pairing finder button sits directly under the store pill — tap it and the Food pairing finder opens as a pop-up over the list (see §14); close it to return to the list.
        • The gear at top right opens Settings.
        • The scan icon sits directly under the gear — tap it to scan a barcode (§4).

        Getting back to the top

        Start scrolling up and a round up-arrow button appears. Tap it to smooth-scroll back to the top. It hides again when you scroll down or reach the top — it is never in your way while you read down the list.

        2Finding a wineSearch, filters, brands and price

        Search

        Type in the Search box — it matches brand, product name or varietal. The line underneath tells you where you stand, e.g. Showing 226 of 226 products · Store 358. Clear the search to bring the full list back.

        Filters

        Tap Filters ▾ to open the filter panel:

        • Brand — pick one brand from the pull-down list.
        • Sweetness — tap it to open its dropdown, then tap levels to toggle them on or off: selected levels go plum with a checkmark, and the dropdown stays open while you pick. The list shows wines matching any selected level; with nothing selected the filter is off. Tap the button again, or anywhere outside the dropdown, to close it. The levels are listed in this order: Extra Dry, Dry, Off-Dry, Medium, then Extra Sweet and Sweet (the sweet pair runs sweetest first). Sorting by Sweetness uses that same order, and wines at the same sweetness sit in product A–Z order.
        • Style / Richness — pick one style, or All reds (Light, Medium, Medium-Full Bodied and Rich Red) or All whites (Light, Medium, Rich and Extra Rich White). Rosé and Cider stay under their own options.
        • On sale — only wines with a sale price.
        • Vegan-friendly — only wines confirmed vegan-friendly (§3).
        • Gluten-safe — only gluten-safe wines.
        • ♥ Loved — only wines you have loved (§6).
        • Under a price — set a maximum price. While that filter is on, results sort most expensive first, down to the cheapest, with unpriced wines last. Clear the filter and the normal order comes back.
        Fastest path to one wineIf you have the bottle in hand, don’t type — scan it (§4). A successful scan clears your other filters and shows just that one wine, fully expanded.
        3Reading a product cardBadges, sugar, sweetness, richness and tasting notes

        Each wine is a card: brand in purple at the top, then the product name, price, and everything you need to answer a customer.

        Badges you may see

        VQAGluten-safeNot in planoVegan-friendlyIn cooler⚡ Flash Sale
        • VQA — VQA Ontario wine.
        • Gluten-safe — safe for a gluten-free customer.
        • Not in plano — not on the current planogram. It stays on the list in case it comes back — it is not a mistake.
        • Vegan-friendly — confirmed vegan-friendly. The Notes for that wine say where the determination came from.
        • ⚡ Flash Sale — the black-and-yellow badge for a short scheduled flash sale (e.g. Black Friday), shown beside the Sale badge on the card and in the details while that sale runs (§9).
        • Unavailable — clearly marked when your store has marked it unavailable (§8). That mark is for your store only.

        The fields

        SizeBottle or box size, e.g. 750mL, 1.5L, 3L, 4L. The same wine in two sizes is two separate entries — details can differ between sizes.
        Sugar (RS)Residual sugar in grams per litre (g/L). Lower is drier. Sugar is not copied between sizes — a 750mL and a 3L of the same wine can genuinely differ.
        SweetnessThe plain-language dryness label, e.g. Extra Dry, Dry, Medium, Sweet. All BASK wines are Extra Dry.
        RichnessBody and colour together, exactly as printed on the shelf tag — e.g. Light White, Medium Red, Rich Red.
        VarietalThe grape or blend, where known.
        Tannins · AcidityLow / Medium / High, where known. A dash (—) means it hasn’t been recorded yet, not that it’s zero.

        Richness colours

        Medium WhiteRoséRich Red

        White wines carry a blue indicator, rosés a pink one, so you can spot the style at a glance while scanning a long list.

        Tasting notes

        Tap tasting notes ▾ on a card to expand it. The expanded view also shows the wine’s product ID — quote that number if you ever report a problem with a listing. Tap again to collapse.

        Notes belong to the wine above themThe Notes area sits under its own wine’s details. If you’re ever unsure which wine a note belongs to, it’s always the product directly above the note.
        4Barcode scannerScan a bottle straight to its card
        1. Tap the scan icon under the settings gear, top right.
        2. The scanner opens full-screen using the rear camera. Hold the barcode inside the viewfinder and hold steady — it focuses continuously where your phone supports it.
        3. Tap the ← back arrow at the top left to go back.

        When it recognises the barcode

        You jump straight to that product: your other filters clear, the wine’s brand, name and size appear in the Search box, and the list shows just that one wine, fully expanded — as if you had searched for it. Clear the search to restore the full list.

        “Barcode not on file”

        If the barcode isn’t linked to any product yet, a prompt says so and shows the number you scanned. From there you can:

        • Pick the right product from the list and tap Link barcode — the link saves to the shared list, so that barcode works on everyone’s phone from then on.
        • Tap Add as a new product if the wine isn’t listed at all (§8).
        • Tap Cancel to do neither.

        Camera can’t read it?

        Use the typed-barcode fallback on the scanner screen — type the digits under the barcode and look it up that way. If the scanner can’t read any digits at all, it tells you so and points you to the typed option rather than failing silently.

        If a link won’t saveThe app says clearly when a barcode link can’t be saved. Note the barcode number and the product it belongs to, and let Michael know — don’t keep re-scanning and hoping.
        5StoresSwitching stores, adding one, and store types

        Switching store

        Tap the number-only pill beside the heading (e.g. 358) and pick another store. The list immediately shows what that store carries.

        What is per-store, and what is shared

        Per-storeWhich products the store carries, and which are marked unavailable. Changing these affects only that store.
        Shared by allPrices, notes and product information. Edit a price or a tasting note and every store sees it.

        The shared list refreshes itself about every 30 seconds while the app is open, so changes made on another phone appear without reloading.

        Adding a store

        1. Choose Add store — either in the first-visit popup or in Settings.
        2. Enter the store number and choose a store type: Loblaws, Sobeys, Foodland, or Non-boutique.
        3. The new store starts empty. Go to Settings → Store settings → Set store products and tick the products it carries from the checkbox list.

        Store types and impact documents

        • Loblaws stores see the Legacy Loblaws impact in Documents: the current impact cheat sheet, the full P8/P9 PDFs, and “What’s on sample today.” Store 358 is a Loblaws store.
        • Sobeys, Foodland, Non-boutique and any custom type see a note that their impact isn’t loaded yet.
        • Store settings in Settings is a collapsible section — tap its heading to expand it. It shows your current store’s type, the list of types, and an Add new store type button if Michael adds more.
        6Loving wines ♥Hearts, Most loved, and your Loved wines list

        Loving a wine is your personal thumbs-up — your recommendations to each other. You must be signed in to love (§11); browsing never requires it.

        • The heart sits near the three-dots menu on each card.
        • Hollow heart = you haven’t loved it. Filled red heart = you have. Tap to toggle.
        • A wine’s card shows “Loved by X merchants” directly under its badge line — but only when X is above zero. No line at all means nobody has loved it yet.
        • The most-loved wine in the list earns a Most loved badge.

        Your Loved wines list

        In Documents → Loved wines you’ll find only the wines you’ve loved, most loved first. Tap one to open it. You can also use the ♥ Loved filter (§2) to see them in the main list.

        “Couldn’t save that love”?That message meant the save was refused — it was a database problem (now fixed), not your connection, and it affected every wine the same way. If you ever see it again: note which wine, try once more in a fresh tab, and tell Michael if it persists.
        7Wine commentsThe comment bubble in a wine’s notes

        Every wine can have a conversation attached to it — tasting impressions, customer feedback, “order more of this.” Comments were built not to slow searching down: nothing about comments loads while you search or filter.

        Finding the comments

        • Expand a wine’s notes. The comment icon is in the notes area — comments live there, nowhere else.
        • A number badge beside the icon shows how many comments the wine has — only when there is at least one.
        • Comments stay hidden until you press the icon. Press it to open the thread; press again to put it away.

        Posting, editing, deleting

        • Open the thread and write your comment. Comments show newest first.
        • Your own comments have Edit and Delete — you can fix a typo or remove a comment entirely. You can’t edit or delete anyone else’s.
        • Your name on a comment is your display name if you’ve set one (§11).
        • Comment counts load quietly in the background after the list appears, refresh on the app’s regular 30-second check, and update straight away when a comment on that wine is posted or deleted.
        Comment or note?Notes are the shared facts about the wine (tasting notes, vegan source, and so on). Comments are conversation. If it’s a fact the next person needs, it belongs in the notes via Edit (§8); if it’s an opinion or a heads-up, it’s a comment.
        8Adding & editing productsThe three-dots menu, unavailable, cooler and plano

        Editing is locked behind sign-in — if you’re signed out, you can browse everything but change nothing. Every change is recorded in the change history with your name (§13).

        The three-dots menu

        Tap the ⋮ menu in a card’s top-right corner for:

        • Edit — open the product editor.
        • Mark unavailable / available — for your store only. Other stores are unaffected.
        • Not in plano — flag that the wine isn’t on the planogram. It stays on the list (§3).
        • Cooler on / off — whether this product belongs in the cooler.

        In the editor

        • Varietal is a pull-down list — or choose the add-new option and type a varietal that isn’t listed yet.
        • Barcode field — type or paste a barcode to link it to this product. Links save to the shared list for everyone (§4).
        • Regular price — set or correct the regular price here (§9). Price changes are shared by all stores.
        • Sugar, sweetness, richness, tannins, acidity, tasting notes and notes can all be corrected here. Where a shelf (romance) tag and the web disagree, trust the tag — the tag is what the customer sees.

        Adding a brand-new product

        • Use Add product, or a scan’s Add as a new product.
        • The new wine joins the shared list and your current store at the same time — it’s searchable and scannable straight away, with no separate ticking-in step.
        • It is not added to other stores automatically. Each store ticks it in for itself if it carries it.
        Before you add, search firstThe same wine in a different size is a separate product — but the same wine in the same size is a duplicate. Search the brand and name first so the shared list stays clean.
        9Prices & salesSale / Reg / Save, plus tax & deposit, and the broken-sale flag

        How a sale shows on a card

        • Sale — the price the customer pays now. This is the big price on the card.
        • Reg — the regular price.
        • Save — the difference between the two.

        Not every wine has a price yet — a wine with no price simply shows no price. That’s expected for part of the list, not an error.

        Prices are plus tax & deposit

        Every price in the app is the shelf-tag price — 13% HST and the container deposit are added at the register. On the card, the small muted +tax & dep beside the price says exactly that. Open a product’s details to see both prices, clearly labelled: Tag price (the price as printed on the tag — for a wine on sale, the sale price) and At the register (the total the customer actually pays: tag price + 13% HST + deposit). The HST is charged on the tag price only, never on the deposit. The deposit is 10¢ for glass, PET, Tetra Pak and bag-in-box containers up to 630mL and 20¢ above that; cans are 10¢ up to 1L and 20¢ above that; containers of 100mL or less carry no deposit. So a standard 750mL bottle has a 20¢ deposit, a 355mL can 10¢, and a 375mL bottle 10¢.

        Fixing a price

        • Open the product editor (§8) and set the Regular price. Prices are shared — one correction fixes it for every store.
        • Impact sale prices are locked. Sale prices that come from a period impact document can’t be edited in the app — they follow the impact.

        “Sale price not working”

        If a sale price is set but isn’t displaying or saving properly, use the sale-broken flag on the product to mark it. That flags it for follow-up instead of the problem being silently lost — un-flag it once it’s displaying correctly.

        Flash sales

        Some sales are flash sales — short scheduled sales like the Black Friday Flash Sale (Nov 16–30: Susse Reserve Riesling and JT Grand Reserve Shiraz, $3 off each). A wine in a flash sale carries a black-and-yellow ⚡ Flash Sale badge beside its pink Sale badge — on the card, and again in the expanded details beside the Sale / Reg / Save lines — so a flash sale never just looks like an ordinary sale.

        When an impact sale ends, the sale clears itself

        When a scheduled impact sale period ends, the sale comes off the products in that impact automatically — both the on-sale flag and the sale price are cleared, even if that sale was typed in manually, so a stale sale never lingers past its impact. The regular price is never cleared — only the sale state is. A product that belongs to no impact sale is untouched: a one-off manual sale on it stays until someone turns it off.

        10DocumentsLoved wines, impact sheets, this manual and PDFs

        The Documents tab is a collapsible section — tap its heading to expand or collapse it. Inside:

        • Loved wines — your loved wines, most loved first (§6).
        • This manual — the web version you’re reading now, plus the Manual.pdf for printing. Same content, same version number as the app.
        • Legacy Loblaws impact (Loblaws stores only) — the Current Impact Cheat Sheet, the full P8/P9 impact PDFs, and “What’s on sample today.” Other store types see a note that their impact isn’t loaded yet (§5).
        Which manual should you open?On your phone, the web manual — text fits your screen and search works. The PDF is for the printer: fixed pages, made for paper.
        11Settings & your accountGoogle sign-in, display name, appearance

        Settings opens with your account status first — either the account you’re signed in with, or that you’re not signed in.

        Signing in with Google

        1. In Settings → Account, tap the centred Sign in with Google button.
        2. Complete the Google sign-in. You’ll be returned to the app, signed in.
        3. If you’re already signed into Google on the phone, Google may skip its login screen entirely — that’s normal.
        Why sign in at all?“You’re seeing this because you’re not signed in. You can browse and search without signing in — signing in lets you love wines and add or edit products, so your loves are yours and your changes carry your name.”

        Display name

        Don’t want to appear under your Google account name? Set your own:

        • In Settings → Account, enter a display name (up to 60 characters) and save. You can change it any time.
        • It’s yours only — it never changes anyone else’s name.
        • Your display name is used everywhere your name appears: the Account block, change history, wine comments, suggestions, and the Admin signed-in users list — including renaming your older entries.
        • Clear it with Use my Google name instead to go back to your Google profile name.
        • Once set, it syncs across your devices.

        Appearance

        • Choose Light, Dark, or Auto (Follow phone).
        • Light is the first-open default and is labelled “Default” in the setting. Dark has no label — if it isn’t marked Default, it isn’t the default.
        • Your choice is remembered and respected on reload.

        Also in Settings

        • Store settings — collapsible section with your store type, Set store products, and Add store (§5).
        • Support Center — Wine Rack Store Support Centre contacts (§14).
        • Games & Contests — its own tab at the top of Settings, beside Support; it is the home of the Wine Trivia rapid fire game (§16).
        • Admin — a button at the very bottom of Settings, visible to Michael and appointed admins (§13).
        • The footer line reads “Created and maintained by Michael Benia WR 358.”
        12SuggestionsAsk for a change, track what happened to it

        Found something missing, wrong, or worth adding? Send a suggestion instead of just mentioning it in passing — suggestions are tracked, so they don’t get lost.

        • Write and submit your suggestion — you’ll get a thank-you confirming it landed.
        • Your suggestions lists everything you’ve sent. You can Edit or Delete your own suggestions.
        • When an admin deals with one, they can mark it Acted upon and reply to it — the reply shows with your suggestion, so you can see what was done.
        • You only ever see your own suggestions, not everyone else’s.
        13AdminFor Michael and appointed admins

        Admin lives behind a button at the very bottom of Settings. It is restricted to Michael (halroben8@gmail.com, the default admin) and users he appoints. If you can’t see it, you’re not an admin — that’s expected for most users.

        The signed-in users list

        Admin works from one list: everyone who has logged in — tap Open Signed-in users in the Admin area and it opens in its own window, so the Admin panel itself stays short however many people have signed in. There is no appointing or banning by typing an email address — everything is done with buttons on the person’s row:

        • Make admin — appoint that user as an admin. The button becomes Remove admin once they are one.
        • Ban — block that account. The button becomes Unban; bans are reversible from the same row.

        Select CVQA

        Some bottles are CVQA — competitor VQA — and not every store carries them. Tap Select CVQA in Admin: it opens a checkbox list of every product, ticked bottles are CVQA. Ticked bottles are left out of Guess the Wine, so stores that don’t carry them aren’t at a disadvantage, and typing cvqa in the main search finds them. The flag is shared for all stores. Tick or untick, then tap Save CVQA.

        The safeguards

        • Only Michael can make or remove admins.
        • Michael can never be banned, and nobody can ban themselves.
        • Making/removing an admin and banning/unbanning are all logged.
        • A banned user is signed out with a clear “Account blocked” notice. They can still browse the list, search and filters — but they cannot love, comment, suggest, or add/edit anything. The check runs at sign-in and on the app’s regular 30-second check while it’s open.

        Change history

        • Every add and edit is recorded with who made it (display name if set), what changed, and when.
        • Price edits are recorded with the old and new values — Regular price and Sale price alike, including a sale price typed on a wine that isn’t on sale yet.
        • Tap Open Change history in Admin and the history opens in its own full-screen view — it is no longer a long list inside the Admin panel. The newest change is always on top, the list scrolls inside that view, and Refresh reloads it. The back arrow, Back to Admin or the × closes it and returns you to Admin.
        • Clear history, at the bottom of that view, deletes every Change history entry for everyone. It always asks first — tap Clear history, then confirm with Yes, clear history (or Cancel to back out); nothing is deleted on the first tap. After clearing, a confirmation message shows and the view is empty; changes made afterwards are recorded as usual. Clearing can’t be undone.
        • History is Admin-only — it isn’t shown to regular users.
        • Admin also carries the action log for admin actions, and the suggestions queue (Section 12) for marking suggestions acted upon and replying.
        14Support — Food pairing finder & Support Center“What are you eating?”, and who to call at Wine Rack Store Support

        Support Center is at the very top of Settings → Support — the Wine Rack Store Support Centre contacts, described below.

        What’s on sample today? and Wine Knowledge live in Settings → Support only — they are not in Documents. The Support tab holds just three entries: Support Center, What’s on sample today? and Wine Knowledge. The impact documents and this manual stay in Documents.

        Food pairing finder — “What are you eating?” The finder is a pop-up window, never an inline form. One button opens it: the Food pairing finder button under the store pill in the header, and the pop-up opens over the list. There is no Food pairing entry in the Support tab. Close the pop-up (× or Close — back to the list) to return to the list. Type a dish (spicy Thai curry, roast chicken, steak, salmon, chocolate dessert…) and the finder ranks the wines the store you’re viewing actually carries and has available, closest match first with a few backups. Each recommendation gives a reason tailored to the dish you typed, naming the actual element in it: how the wine’s sweetness handles the spice you mentioned, how its acidity cuts the creamy or rich part, how its acidity meets tomato, how its tannins grip grilled meat, how it suits the named fish, or why it stays sweeter than the named dessert — drawn from the wine’s sweetness, acidity, tannins, richness, varietal and tasting notes. It follows the classic rules: sweetness for spicy food, acidity for rich or tomato-based dishes, tannin for red meat, light high-acid whites for fish, and a wine sweeter than the dessert. Wines the store does not carry, and wines marked unavailable at your store, are never recommended. Tap any recommendation to open that wine in the list.

        The app carries the Wine Rack Store Support Centre contact sheet (last updated April 21, 2026) in Settings → Support Center, so it’s in your pocket on the floor — no hunting for the sheet.

        Contacts are grouped the same way as the sheet:

        • Support Services
        • Marketing
        • Operations
        • Marketplace
        • Distribution / Shipment / Store Ordering
        • HR / Payroll / Safety

        Each entry shows the name, phone and email as supplied, with any notes. Tap a phone number to call it; tap an email to write to it.

        15Troubleshooting & FAQThe problems people actually hit

        An old tab is showing an old version

        The app updates often. If something looks out of date or behaves oddly, close the tab and open a fresh one — a tab that’s been open a long while can be running an old version of the app.

        Love won’t stick — “Couldn’t save that love”

        This was a database fault, fixed in version 2026.11.03.9 — hearts displayed fine but no love would save, on any wine. If you see it now: try once in a fresh tab, and if it persists, tell Michael which wine and when. It is not your connection.

        A change didn’t appear in Change history

        This was a database fault, fixed in version 2026.11.03.15 — edits saved fine but no history entry was recorded, on any wine, so Change history showed “No changes recorded yet”. Changes made from version 2026.11.03.15 on are recorded again. If a new change still doesn’t appear: open Change history from Admin, tap Refresh in that view, and if it persists, tell Michael which wine and when. It is not your connection.

        Sign-in doesn’t bring me back to the app

        Sign-in returns you to wherever the app is served from, and the live app address must be allowed in the sign-in settings. If Google sign-in strands you elsewhere, open the live app in a fresh tab and sign in there.

        The store popup keeps appearing

        The “Which store are you at?” popup asks on a fresh open. Pick your store from the list (don’t just close it) so the app knows which list to show you.

        A wine shows one more product than expected

        Check the count line under Search (Showing X of X products). If the total has crept up, a duplicate or an extra product may have been added to the shared list — search the brand to find it and let Michael know rather than adding another copy.

        Scanner opens but doesn’t recognise anything

        Hold the barcode flat, well-lit and inside the viewfinder, and give it a second to focus. Still nothing? Use the typed-barcode fallback on the scanner screen (§4).

        A sale price looks wrong

        Check Reg against the shelf tag — and remember, trust the tag. Correct the regular price in the editor if the tag disagrees with the app (§9); if the sale itself won’t display, set the sale-broken flag.

        The manual PDF needs zooming on my phone

        That’s the PDF, not you — a PDF is a fixed page, so a phone shrinks it to fit. Use this web manual on your phone; keep the PDF for printing.

        Who do I ask?

        For the app itself, send a suggestion (§12) so it’s tracked. For Wine Rack store support, use the Support Center contacts in Settings (§14).

        16Games & Contests — Wine TriviaThe 1-minute rapid fire game, in its own Settings tab

        Settings has a fourth tab, Games & Contests, beside Settings, Documents and Support. It is the home for Grapevine’s games — Wine Trivia — 1-minute rapid fire and Guess the Wine. There is no game button in the header and none in Support; the games live in Games & Contests only. No sign-in is needed to play either game.

        How to play

        1. Open Settings → Games & Contests and tap Wine Trivia — 1-minute rapid fire. The game opens as a pop-up.
        2. Tap Start — 60 seconds. The big timer at the top starts counting down from 60, and the first question appears.
        3. Each question has four answers in a 2×2 grid — tap one. The timer and your live score stay pinned at the top while the questions change underneath.

        Scoring

        • Correct: the button turns green, a ding sounds, your score goes up by one, and the next question comes straight away — no delay.
        • Wrong: the button turns red, a buzzer sounds (and the phone vibrates on Android, where supported), the right answer is shown in green — and the next question waits 3 seconds. The clock keeps running, so a wrong guess costs you real time.
        • When the timer hits zero, the final scoreboard shows how many you got right in that minute, how many you answered in total, and your best score this session. Tap Play again for a fresh run.

        The questions are general wine knowledge — grapes, regions, styles, serving and wine terms from all over the wine world. They are not about any one store and not drawn from any store’s list. The question bank is far bigger than anyone can finish in a minute, the questions are shuffled every run with no repeats, so the timer always ends the game — you can never run out of questions. Your score for a single game lives only in that session — the shared exception is the High Score board below.

        High Score board

        Trivia is a social game, so its high scores are shared — one board for everyone who plays, not just the scores on your own phone. The board shows the top 3 players and what they scored, best first, and it lives only on the game’s own start page, under the Start button — open Wine Trivia to see who you have to beat before you play. There is no separate High Score button. One spot per player: each player appears at most once, with their best score — a new score only replaces your own spot if it beats your best, and a lower score leaves your best standing.

        • When a game ends, if your score makes the top 3, the end screen congratulates you and tells you the place you attained — for example, “Congratulations! You made #3 on the High Score board!”
        • Enter your name and tap Save my score to put it on the board. If you’re signed in, the name field is prefilled with your display name — you can change it before saving; if you’re not signed in, just type a name. No sign-in is needed to be on the board.
        • Tying the current #3 score isn’t quite enough — the earlier #3 was set first, so a new score has to beat it to take the place.
        • The board is stored in the shared list (the trivia_high_scores table). Until that table has been created, the board simply shows that high scores are coming soon or that no scores are on it yet — and the game itself plays exactly the same either way.

        Guess the Wine

        Open Settings → Games & Contests and tap Guess the Wine. Each round shows one wine’s tasting notes, with its sweetness and style as hints, and four bottles to choose from — 10 rounds, no timer, so take time to read properly. The wines come from the store you’re viewing, and only wines whose notes don’t name the brand or product can be the answer (that would give it away). CVQA bottles are left out entirely — see Select CVQA in Admin above — because not every store carries them. Correct answers ding and go green; wrong answers buzz, go red, and show the right bottle. Scores live only in that session — there is no shared board for this game.

        Typing cvqa in the main search lists the CVQA bottles.

        Winerack Contests

        Below Wine Trivia in the same tab is Winerack Contests, marked Coming soon. It is a placeholder for now: tapping it just shows a “Coming soon” note — it does not open a form and does not submit or save anything yet.

        No sound? The game’s sounds are switched on by your tap on Start (phones require a tap before any sound can play). If it’s still quiet, check the phone isn’t on silent or turned down — the game itself has no mute switch.

        WR Product Info — Manual, Version 2026.11.04.15
        Created and maintained by Michael Benia WR 358
        This web manual and the print PDF carry the same content and the same version as the app.

        Edit product

        Separate from the Regular price above — both prices can always be seen and entered here. The Sale price is the price shown as the “Sale” line while On sale is Yes.

        Tap “Scan barcode with camera” to scan a barcode straight into the field instead of typing it, type or paste a new barcode to replace the registered one, or use Clear barcode to remove the link. Scanning fills the field and brings you back here — tap Save to register it. Saving updates the shared list for everyone: the new barcode will open this product, and the old one will no longer open it.

        Price, tasting notes and product info are global — shared by every store. Availability and In cooler are the exceptions: they are per store, so those settings here only change this product for the store you're viewing.

        Add store

        Ticking only sets which products this store carries, chosen from the one shared product list. Price, notes and product info are global — shared by all stores — and are never changed or copied per store here. Cooler status is per store: a new store starts with all cooler values blank, and each product's cooler status is set for that store afterwards — it is never copied from Store 358 or any other store. Saving a store here updates the shared list, so every user sees the same stores and the same products in each.

        Which store are you at?

        Pick your store from the dropdown to see that store's products. If your store isn't in the list yet, choose Add store in the dropdown and we'll create it for you.

        New store? Once it's created, use the Settings gear (top right) → “Set store products” to tick the products it carries. A new store starts with all cooler values blank — cooler status differs store to store, so set each product's cooler status for the new store afterwards.

        Scan barcode

        Barcode not on file

        This barcode isn’t linked to a product yet.

        Pick the product it belongs to to link it, so the next scan goes straight to that product.

        Sign in first

        Sign in with Google to continue.

        Loves are saved to your account, and changes are tagged with your name so the team can see who loved and changed what. Sign-in is required to use this app.

        Suggestions

        Leave a comment or suggestion for the moderator. It’s sent with your name and email. Only you, the moderator and appointed admins can read your suggestions — yours are listed under the form, where you can edit or delete them, and see when one has been acted upon or replied to.
